long_biography.plain_text:
A pharmacy degree prepared Francesco Angelini for more than a ceremonial place in the family business. He joined after graduating in 1968, developed its Spanish and Portuguese operations, and led Fater as the consumer-goods company strengthened its market position. When his father died in 1993, Angelini became group chairman.

His tenure combined pharmaceutical growth with deliberate diversification. A joint venture with Procter & Gamble expanded the household-products platform, while acquisitions added wine and fragrance businesses to the portfolio. Angelini also formalised the group's holding structure and supported a family foundation. Outside business he pursued bridge at international championship level, turning a competitive interest into a second sustained public identity. He later transferred control to his daughter Thea Paola while retaining a minority stake and additional economic rights.
